text.p: Britain's biggest clothing retailer Marks and Spencer Plc on Thursday announced an expansion in British town centres with the purchase of 19 stores from Littlewoods for 192.5 million pounds ($323 million) cash.
The retailer unveiled the deal at its annual shareholder meeting along with first quarter trading figures which showed clothing sales up by nearly 10 percent.
Littlewoods, the privately owned retail-to-football pools group, last month abandoned plans to sell its entire chain of 135 high-street stores, saying it would instead sell off only selected sites.

There had been speculation in the press that Littlewoods, owned by the secretive millionaire Moores family, was about to clinch a deal for 19 of its shops, and had been in talks with M&S, Boots Co Plc and Next Plc.
M&S chairman Sir Richard Greenbury told the annual meeting the deal would enhance shareholder value.
"This outstanding opportunity gives us an extra 600,000 square feet of selling space in key town and city centres, which again underlines our confidence in the future of the high street," he said.
The group expects to start fitting out the stores next February and intends to begin opening them progressively through the year.

The stores are in Bath, Belfast in Northern Ireland, Bromley, Cardiff, Carlisle, Chester, Derby, Edinburgh, Ilford, Kingston, Leeds, London, Dudley, Newcastle, Norwich, Peterborough, Shrewbury, Watford and Worcester.
Greenbury said the encouraging first quarter performance suggested the group was heading for another year of good progress.
Food sales were up 2.3 percent, adjusted for Easter, and in June and July were running 3.5 percent ahead of last year.
"With price deflation approaching 1.5 percent throuhout the period the volume increase has, therefore, remained strong," he said.

On the last month's UK government budget statement, Greenbury said the company was looking into the impact of the abolition of dividend tax credits on its pension fund and assessing the precise costs involved.
Greenbury said the reduction in corporation tax to 31 percent from 33 percent in the budget would improve the group's UK profits after tax by about 20 million pounds.
M&S's shares stood six pence higher at 593 pence.

Analysts said the trading figures were quite good on clothing considering the wet weather in June. "What's really encouraging is that they've got a decent slug of Littlewood's stores," said one analyst.
